game.name: Dungreed
game.short_description: Dungreed is a 2D side-scrolling action game with 2D Rogue-LITE elements. You become an adventurer exploring a continuously evolving dungeon to prevent the town from being destroyed. Eliminate enemies, use a variety of weapons and magic, eat food, and defeat evil in the dungeon!

other_scores.source: Nintendo Life (Switch review, listed on Metacritic)

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Dungreed is a 2D action roguelite dungeon crawler where you explore rooms, fight enemies and collect weapons and items. He calls it a hidden gem that looks basic on Steam but turns out to have a huge amount of content and polish. He praises its smooth controls, weapon variety, food mechanic, bosses and music. He places it at the very top of A tier, just short of S.
praise: Controls and movement feel very smooth, with good dashes and a lot of player control
Large weapon pool where each weapon feels very different, with many unique synergies
Food system lets you eat different foods during a run to gain stats and focus on one stat
Items and passives all change gameplay mechanically rather than being plain number bumps
Bosses are phenomenal and the music is hilariously good
Multiple characters and lots of customization
Developers released a big free update years later with a hidden boss, new area, new weapons and a hard mode with unique enemies
criticism: Nothing explicitly criticised; he only says it falls just short of S tier, which he reserves for the very best
Looks basic on first impression, which hides how much depth it has (hidden-gem problem)
unique_points: Food mechanic moves basic stat adjustments like attack speed onto food choices, leaving items free to be mechanics-changing
Surprise large free post-launch update years after release for fans, including new boss, location and hard mode
commentary.quote: it's almost an S tier but s tier is really for the best of the best
comparisons: Other 2D action roguelikes (general comparison on movement and combat feel)
design_criteria: Controls/game feel: smooth movement, dashes and combat compared with clunky 2D action roguelikes
Weapon diversity: many weapons each very different
Synergies: many unique item and weapon synergies
Item design: items and passives change gameplay rather than just numbers
Stat/build customization: food mechanic for focusing stats
Boss design: bosses described as phenomenal
Content and replayability: multiple characters, hard mode, free expansion

community.one_liner: A 2D side-scrolling, mouse-aimed action roguelite by TEAM HORAY (Steam, Feb 2018) where you dash and jump through procedurally assembled dungeons, collect weapons and accessories, manage a hunger/food system, and buy permanent stat upgrades between runs.
community.consensus_summary: Dungreed is a long-running indie favourite on PC: Steam shows roughly 9,600 reviews at about 93% positive (Very Positive), and the positive reviews come from players with very high playtime (often 50-250 hours) who praise weapon and build variety, snappy dash-based combat and the Workshop mods. Critic coverage is thin: Metacritic has no Metascore (only one Nintendo Life review of the Switch port, 80) and a tiny Switch user score of 7.2 from 5 ratings. The complaints are consistent: awkward keyboard/mouse and controller handling, repeated items and thin area variety, RNG-driven balance where lucky builds trivialise the game and unlucky ones are stuck, and bullet-hell late bosses. Steam reviewers say the developer has moved on to Sephiria, so content updates appear to have slowed, but the modding scene keeps it alive. Note: this research was done with WebSearch unavailable (session search budget exhausted), so critic/community coverage relies on Steam data, Metacritic, and the Steam community pages rather than Reddit or major outlets.
best_things: Huge weapon and accessory pool that synergises into many different builds; several reviewers cite 'god runs' from item combinations
Fast, snappy dash-based movement and combat that feels good once a build comes together (one reviewer likens the movement approach to Rogue Legacy)
Character customisation per run, with many valid playstyles and a difficulty curve that adds new content gradually
Food/hunger system: buying food for buffs fills a hunger meter that drains, forcing you to budget stat gains against saving room for better food
No contact damage from enemies, which one reviewer singled out as a relief
Active Steam Workshop: custom weapons, characters and even items imported from Sephiria extend replay value (reviewers call the Workshop community 'legends')
Strong value at about $10 and good long-tail engagement, with many players returning every few months
Pixel-art style and movement praised by several reviewers (one calls it a personal favourite 2D roguelike)
worst_things: Controls draw the harshest complaints: aiming and dashing follow the mouse pointer so keyboard players dash the wrong way, and keybinding/settings menus were reported as broken by some
Controller support is inconsistent: one PS5-controller user reports the game flipping between Xbox and 'Undefined' input mid-run; others say it plays best on a gamepad
Item and loot rotation feels repetitive: the same items recur in shops and chests, so the large library feels smaller than it is, and there is low visual variety across areas

Balance is swingy: lucky weapon/evasion/block combos make you near-invincible while a poor-loot run leaves you with weak items; some legendary items are reported weaker than commons and some characters feel underpowered

Late bosses are bullet sponges that flood the screen with projectiles; one complaint notes a boss using red/orange/brown projectiles in a red/orange/brown hell stage where attacks blend into the background
Enemy attack timings feel slow compared with the very fast player and spam-attack weapons, making dodging feel jarring (detailed in one long negative review)
Bland, minimal story and lore according to several reviewers
improvements: Better input handling: a working rebinding menu and reliable controller detection (PS controllers especially)
More permanent upgrades or meta-progression to help struggling players, since progression tops out and later success is skill plus RNG
Better item rotation/pool management so shops and chests do not keep showing the same items
More area and visual variety, and more enemy/boss diversity to reduce repetitiveness
Rebalancing rarity and weak characters so legendary items and unorthodox builds are not punished; clearer guaranteed healing rather than mostly RNG healing
Fix or clarify achievement bugs (one 100% player reports the final food-eating achievement not unlocking) and quest progress not carrying across a single run
unique_things: Food/hunger meter as a build-management resource: buffs are bought and limited by stomach capacity, which is unusual for the genre
2D mouse-aimed shooter/melee hybrid platformer with a dash-centred movement kit and no contact damage
Town-rebuilding and training meta layer: permanent stat training plus unlockable vendors and NPCs rescued from the dungeon
Active Steam Workshop scene adding custom characters and weapons to a game with a simple pixel-art pipeline
Available on PC, Switch, PS4 and iOS
tedious_or_disliked: Achievement hunting and the optional true final boss: reviewers describe completion as long, repetitive and in places annoying (one says the true boss looked more annoying than satisfying)
Repeated runs through the same few areas, with a lack of area variety, leads to fatigue after dozens of runs
Spending runs with only low-rarity gear and no healing is frustrating once meta-progression is maxed out
Bullet-hell late stages and projectile-spamming bosses become a slog rather than a skill test for some
Keyboard controls and cursor-relative dashing cause cheap hits, making the keyboard experience a chore
divisive_points: Difficulty and balance: some call it 'pretty easy' and relaxing, others call it punishing and skill-only with poorly balanced RNG
Depth and longevity: fans put in 100-250 hours and call it a gold-standard roguelite, while others see a generic, shallow, cheap-feeling roguelite that falls flat after 15-20 runs
Controls and game feel: praised as crisp and snappy (especially on controller) by many, described as awkward or unintuitive by others, partly due to the 2.5D perspective and mouse-relative aiming
Item pool: 'massive loot library' versus 'same items keep showing up'
community.reception_notes: Launched on Steam on Feb 14, 2018 from a small Korean indie team and built a durable audience through word of mouth and content updates; later ports reached Nintendo Switch, PS4 and iOS (per Metacritic). Critics barely covered it: Metacritic shows only one critic review (Nintendo Life, 80), so no Metascore, and the Switch user score of 7.2 is based on 5 ratings. Steam's all-time rating sits around 93% positive on roughly 9.6k reviews, with recent reviews also positive. Reviewers in 2025-2026 say updates have largely stopped as the developer shifted to Sephiria, but the Workshop community continues to add content. Recurring technical issues reported in negative reviews include input/keybinding bugs and controller misdetection. SteamSpy-style data in the local file lists roughly 200k-500k owners, which, together with the revenue estimate, is order-of-magnitude only. No OpenCritic page could be found (OpenCritic fetches failed or returned an unrelated game).
